articles.title: India's first 100% indigenised AK-203 'Sher' rifle made, test-fired at factory in UP's Amethi
articles.content: India has manufactured and tested a prototype of the 100 per cent indigenised AK-203 ‘Sher’ rifle, with army trials for the weapon to begin in September this year, Major General SK Sharma said on Sunday, while sharing a video of the test firing. Ever single component and input material which has gone into manufacturing the rifle is sourced from the Indian industry, Major Gen Sharma said. (LinkedIn/ Maj Gen SK Sharma, AVSM, SM(Bar), VSM) The rifles are manufactured by the Indo-Russian Rifles Private Limited, a joint-venture of the Indian Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs), along with Concern Kalashnikov and Rosoboron export from Russia. Maj Gen S K Sharma, who is the CEO and managing director of IRRPL, said the testing of the prototype was “a moment of immense pride” for the company. ₹1,577 crore">Also Read | Indian Army to get loitering munitions worth ₹ 1,577 crore “We have successfully produced and fired the first AK-203 (Sher) rifle made with 100% Indian components and input materials,” Major Gen Sharma said in a post on LinkedIn. ‘Every single component, input material sourced from India’ Read More He said the prototype of the first 100 per cent indigenised vehicle had “successfully undergone firing, including burst firing”, adding that the initial results were “extremely encouraging.” “A proud moment for IRRPL, our partners (AWEIL & OSL) and MSMEs, and the entire Indian Defence Industry. This is Atmanirbhar Bharat in action!!” Major Gen Sharma said. Also Read | India imposes phased ban on import of 405 defence items to boost domestic production ‘IRRPL moving towards production rate of one AK-203 every 100 seconds’ Major Gen Sharma said that with the successful testing of the first prototype, IRRPL would now focus on producing the requisite number of 100 per cent indigenised AK-203 ‘Sher’ rifles for trials to the Indian Armed Forces in September, 2026. The IRRPL CEO said the company will be “moving towards a production rate of one AK-203 (Sher) every 100 seconds,” adding that there is “much more ahead.” Major Gen Sharma further said that IRRPL was also looking to prepone the delivery timeline of the approximately 6 lakh rifles that it has to supply to the Indian Army “by almost one year”. He credited the company's efforts towards “capacity enhancement, indigenisation and production optimisation” for the efficiency. IRRPL is mandated under a ₹ 5,200 crore contract to supply 6,01,427 rifles to the armed forces by October 2032. However, Major Gen Sharma had earlier too said that the company plans to finish deliveries by December 2030. articles.title: AssamSAT moves closer to implementation as partner selection enters final stage
articles.content: News Assam AssamSAT moves closer to implementation as partner selection enters final stage: Himanta Biswa Sarma AssamSAT moves closer to implementation as partner selection enters final stage: Himanta Biswa Sarma AssamSAT has entered the final stage of implementation as Assam evaluates partner bids. The project is expected to bring Earth observation data into governance and development planning. Advertisement India TodayNE Aug 23, 2026 , Updated Aug 23, 2026, 5:24 PM IST Follow us: Story highlights The state invited bids under the Design, Build, Launch, Operate framework Private space companies from across India showed strong interest in the project Dedicated committees are evaluating proposals before the government selects its partner Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma has announced that the state’s AssamSAT, described as India’s first state-led Earth Observation satellite system, has entered a crucial stage of implementation. Sharing the update on National Space Day, Sarma said the Assam government had earlier invited Expressions of Interest (EoI) to select an implementation partner under the DBLOTT model — Design, Build, Launch, Operate, Train and Transfer. He said the initiative received strong interest from private space-sector companies across India. Proposals submitted by prospective partners are now being evaluated by dedicated committees as the government moves towards the final stage of partner selection. Sarma described AssamSAT as a significant shift in the state’s approach to space technology, saying Assam would move from being only a user of satellite data to becoming an active participant in the space-tech ecosystem. According to the Chief Minister, the satellite system is expected to support faster, evidence-based governance by providing access to Earth observation data for various developmental and administrative requirements. The initiative is being positioned as a landmark step towards integrating space technology into governance and development planning in Assam. articles.title: PM Modi calls for India to become global hub for space talent and innovation
articles.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday interacted with chief executives of Indian space startups, highlighting the need for policy consistency, global competitiveness and an ecosystem capable of attracting talent from across the world as India’s private space sector expands rapidly. During the interaction, Modi lauded entrepreneurs for taking risks in a relatively new sector and for placing their trust in the government after the opening up of the space industry to private participation. Advertisement The Prime Minister emphasised that predictable policymaking was essential to encourage innovation and risk-taking. He said entrepreneurs should have confidence that policies would remain stable and that they would not be left unsupported when ventures faced difficulties. Advertisement “Whatever decisions we take, we should remain consistent with them and should not keep changing them repeatedly,” Modi said. The interaction featured discussions with CEOs of startups working on launch vehicles, satellite propulsion, orbital services, space debris removal, in-orbit refuelling, ground stations and pharmaceutical manufacturing in space. One entrepreneur from Skyroot described the company as India’s first space-tech unicorn and referred to the successful July 18 launch of India’s first private rocket, which deployed satellites. The CEO said the achievement was only a “warm-up” and the beginning of the company’s larger journey. The company aims to undertake one launch every month by the middle of next year, the CEO said, adding that it had already established three factories and created capacity to produce one rocket a month. Its longer-term ambitions include one launch a week and eventually multiple launches a day. Modi also sought to know whether the success of the first launch had strengthened investor confidence and created opportunities for other startups. The CEOs said confidence among investors had increased, while another entrepreneur said the company had received eight launch contracts in the previous month, most of them from international customers. “The world must now be looking for Indian startups, asking who is there in this field. Because once there is a breakthrough, people’s attention immediately turns towards it,” Modi observed. The Prime Minister also focused on the possibility of India becoming a global destination for space talent. He noted that Indian professionals working in the US and Europe were increasingly looking to return and join companies in India following the opening up of the sector. “We should create an aura that makes people across the world look to India to build their future,” Modi said, adding that people around the world should feel that India was the place to come if they wanted to build a career in the space sector. “I firmly believe that, because of you, we can attract the entire talent pool like a magnet, and that can become a very great strength for us,” he said. articles.title: Sprite and IRCTC launch India's first branded train
articles.content: Sprite and the Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation ( IRCTC ) have launched the Sprite Tejas Express , marking the first branded train partnership for Sprite in India. The train will operate on the Lucknow-New Delhi-Lucknow route for six months from August 2026. The train was flagged off in the presence of senior leadership from Indian Railways, IRCTC and Coca-Cola India . The partnership aims to bring Sprite’s brand experience into the rail travel environment while connecting with passengers travelling for business, leisure and family purposes. Five coaches of the Tejas Express will feature Sprite branding on their exteriors. The train will also be announced as the Sprite Tejas Express at originating and en route stations on both legs of the journey. Onboard, Sprite will be included as part of the passenger food bundle . The launch also featured Sprite sampling and merchandise for passengers, with further brand-led activities planned during the six-month association. Abhishek Gupta, Vice President, Customer Development, Coca-Cola India & Southwest Asia, said, “We congratulate IRCTC on this innovative partnership and an important milestone for travel experiences in India. At Coca-Cola, we continue to explore collaborations that can unlock new avenues for growth and create shared value. Our association with IRCTC reflects our commitment to building long-term customer relationships and expanding our presence across the travel ecosystem. With the Sprite Tejas Express, we are bringing Sprite’s refreshment and creating a more engaging experience for travellers.” The partnership also incorporates recycled materials into the passenger experience. Station benches made from recycled plastic each repurpose approximately 45 kg of post-consumer packaging waste. The ceremonial flag used during the launch was also made from repurposed PET bottles. Ajit Kumar Sinha, Chief Regional Manager, Lucknow Division, IRCTC, said, “At IRCTC, we continuously look at opportunities to enhance the passenger experience across our premium train services through relevant partnerships and initiatives. Our association with Sprite on the Tejas Express brings an established consumer brand into the travel environment through an integrated onboard experience. We look forward to making the journey more engaging for passengers travelling on the Lucknow–New Delhi route.” Sprite has also partnered with Wow! Momo as part of the Sprite Tejas Express experience, extending the brand’s association with food and travel.

articles.title: PM Modi urges private space sector to build 'global aura of innovation'
articles.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has stressed creating an aura around the private sector in space research so that people worldwide feel that if they want to make a career, they should go to India. In an interaction with CEOs and founders of 20 space startups on Friday, Modi also highlighted India's cost-competitiveness in launching space ventures. He emphasised that the country's vast talent pool and high risk-taking capacity would allow India to rapidly establish a dominant position in the global space sector, according to the transcript of the interaction, which was released on Sunday. The prime minister said the world must now be looking for Indian startups – wondering who is leading in this space. Because whenever a breakthrough happens, people's attention shifts immediately, he said. One of the CEOs told the prime minister that after India opened the space industry for private players, a very positive trend was observed and many Indian citizens living in the US and Europe now want to return and work in the country. In response, Modi said: “We need to connect with many people – people who went abroad are now returning. I believe we should create an aura where people worldwide feel that if they want to make a career, they should go to India.” He said such people from across the globe should feel that they should connect with a startup in India, connect with a space agency in India. “I firmly believe that because of you, we can attract the entire talent pool like a magnet, and that can become a massive strength for us,” Modi said. The prime minister appreciated the CEOs of space startups who showed courage by entering a new sector, and said the biggest factor was that they trusted the government's word. “My view has always been that whatever decision we make, we must remain consistent and avoid making frequent changes. This ensures that anyone willing to take a risk feels confident that while a mistake on their end might cause issues, no one will abandon them. Creating that trust was our effort,” he said. Modi also said that India is highly competitive in terms of cost and there is no question about talent. “We are very competitive on cost; there is no question at all about talent, and our people naturally have a higher risk-taking capacity anyway. Because of these, we can establish our place very rapidly,” he said. The CEOs said India's first space-tech unicorn, Skyroot Aerospace, successfully launched India's first private rocket into orbit, and that was just the beginning. By mid-2027, they are aiming for one launch per month, the CEOs said. They thanked the prime minister for opening up the space sector for private players, saying so far, factories have been built with a capacity of one rocket per month. articles.title: Indian space start-up eyes pharma manufacturing in space , satellite recovery to Earth
articles.content: NEW Delhi: A day may not be far away when Indian satellites manufacture pharmaceuticals in space and return them to Earth. While it may sound futuristic, this remarkable possibility was recently shared with Prime Minister Narendra Modi by a young CEO of a space start-up . An Indian space start-up is working on satellites capable of travelling into space, manufacturing pharmaceuticals there and returning them to Earth. A young CEO, who introduced himself as Antariksha, and his co-founder Monika, who attended an interaction with Prime Minister Narendra Modi on August 21, informed him about the venture. The CEO said his company was India’s first space-pharma start-up. “We are making satellites that can go to space, manufacture pharmaceuticals there, and bring them back from space,” he told the Prime Minister. The start-up is developing satellites capable of manufacturing pharmaceutical products in the microgravity environment of space before bringing them back to Earth. Another CEO assured the Prime Minister that his start-up was working towards developing the capacity to launch at least one rocket a month, with the longer-term goal of launching one rocket a week and eventually several rockets a day. Elated and visibly confident about the capabilities of India’s young space start-ups, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, during his recent interaction with 20 CEOs and founders of space start-ups, encouraged them to create an aura that would make people across the world look to India to build their future. The PM assured that the government will never let go of entrepreneurs' hands. Those who take risks will get full support. Skyroot's goal to launch a rocket every month Skyroot informed PM Modi that on July 18, satellites were successfully placed in orbit from India's first private rocket. The company has now set up 3 factories, which have the capacity to build one rocket every month. The company's plan is to launch one rocket every month. The next target is one every week and in the future, several rockets every day. Hyderabad's Skyroot Aerospace launched India's first private orbital rocket Vikram-1 on Saturday, July 18. After this successful launch, PM Modi spoke with the startup founder over the phone. Petrol pumps, cleaning robots and medicine-making satellites Indian startups are working on several new technologies: Space Petrol Pump: A company is developing docking and refueling technology that will refuel satellites in space itself. Debris Removal: Work is underway on a robotic spacecraft that will capture useless and 'dead' satellites floating in space and remove them from orbit. Space Pharma: A startup is preparing satellites that will manufacture medicines in space's zero-gravity and bring them to Earth. Learn about Space Petrol Pump and Space Pharma Just like we go to a pump when our vehicle runs out of petrol on the road, similarly satellites run out of fuel in space. An Indian company is developing technology that will connect with satellites flying in the air and refuel them like petrol-diesel. This will prevent satellites worth crores from becoming useless. Meanwhile, when a medicine is made on Earth, due to the pull of gravity, its chemicals and proteins don't mix properly or start settling down. In contrast, in space, medicines and proteins mix in pure form without any pull. This makes the process of making medicines extremely precise and clean. articles.title: Bengaluru East Division police holds peace meeting ahead of Eid milad,St.Mary's Feast and ...
articles.content: Pramesh S Jain Ahead of the upcoming Eid Milad,St.Mary’s Feast and Ganesh Festival,Bengaluru East Division Police on Saturday held a coordination and peace meeting to ensure the festivals are celebrated peacefully and without inconvenience to the public. The meeting was held at Jalsa Banquet Hall, Pulakeshinagar,and was attended by the Bengaluru City Police Commissioner,Joint Commissioner of Police (East),DCP East,DCP Traffic East and senior officials from BESCOM,civic corporations,BMRCL,Forest Department,BWSSB,BMTC,Fire and Emergency Services and the Health Department. More than 250 people participated, including members of the Eid Milad Committee,St.Mary’s Basilica Feast Committee and various Ganeshotsava committees, besides religious leaders,public representatives and members of the public. Police and officials discussed arrangements to ensure that all three festivals are conducted with mutual respect,brotherhood and communal harmony. Officials issued instructions to take adequate precautionary measures, prevent untoward incidents, maintain law and order and minimise inconvenience to the public. Representatives of different religious communities assured the police of their cooperation in maintaining peace and social unity. Police also appealed to citizens not to believe or spread rumours and to immediately alert the authorities about any suspicious activity or incident. Officials from all concerned departments assured that necessary arrangements would be made for the smooth conduct of the festivals.
